candidates.name: Pressure Washing Quote, Contract & Collection Kit
candidates.segment: Pressure washing: quoting, contracts and payments
candidates.problem: Solo pressure washers spend hours building quotes and contracts from scratch, underprice jobs because they do not know their real cost per sq ft and per gallon of solution, and chase unpaid invoices
candidates.productIdea: Markdown guide on quoting, contracts and collections with a worked example solved step by step (sq ft, gallons, labor hours, USD), plus CSV fill-in worksheets: job cost calculator, quote log, service agreement template, and invoice and payment tracker. No spreadsheet tabs or formulas; the guide's worked example shows the math
candidates.whyNow: Customers now expect fast written quotes and signed agreements, and most solo operators still run their business through texts and phone calls with no software
candidates.demandEvidence: Qualitative signal: recurring posts in pressure washing business communities asking how to price driveways, decks and storefronts by sq ft and how to get paid after the job. No search volume data; to be validated with the queries below
candidates.distributionPath: Pressure washing business Facebook groups and YouTube, with a free job cost worksheet as lead magnet

selectionRationale: Candidate 1 wins with score 74, ahead of #2 (63, HOA board kit) and #10 (58, startup guide). It is the revised version of the previous proposal, reworked as the feedback asked: everything in English including the product name, sq ft, gallons and USD instead of m2, Markdown and CSV only, CSV fill-in worksheets with no tabs or formulas, a worked step-by-step example in the guide, and a focus on quoting, contracts and collection. Against #2, the HOA kit has higher willingness to pay, but its B2B board sales have long cycles and a new seller has no audience there, while the quoting kit reaches solo operators where they already ask these exact questions. Against #10, the startup guide targets an entry-level question with a lot of free content, while the quote, contract and collection problem is tied directly to money the operator is losing today. Main risk: the buyer is a niche of solo operators in one trade, so distribution depends on pressure washing communities; the three queries will validate demand.
